title: Startup Probes – Give Slow Apps Time 🐢
description: Protect slow‑starting containers from premature liveness kills.

slides.title: The Slow Start Problem 🐌
slides.content:
# When initialDelaySeconds isn’t enough

Some applications (JVM, legacy monoliths) can take minutes to start. You can’t set `initialDelaySeconds` on liveness to an extreme value because it delays detection of actual deadlocks later.

**Startup probes** solve this: they run **first**. Until the startup probe succeeds, liveness and readiness probes are not started. This lets you set a `failureThreshold * periodSeconds` that covers the maximum expected startup time.

slides.title: Startup Probe Example 📝
slides.content:
## Configure a long grace period

```yaml
startupProbe:
  httpGet:
    path: /ready
    port: 8080
  periodSeconds: 10
  failureThreshold: 30   # up to 300 seconds (5 min)
livenessProbe:
  httpGet:
    path: /live
    port: 8080
  periodSeconds: 10
  failureThreshold: 3
readinessProbe:
  httpGet:
    path: /health
    port: 8080
  periodSeconds: 5
  failureThreshold: 2
```

If the startup probe hasn’t succeeded after 30 tries (300s), the container is restarted. Once it succeeds, liveness and readiness take over.

quizData.question: When are liveness probes activated?
quizData.explanation: Startup probe gates liveness and readiness; they are disabled until startup succeeds.

slides.title: Pod with All Three Probes
slides.codeSnippet:
containers:
- name: slow-app
  image: java-app:1.0
  startupProbe:
    httpGet:
      path: /started
      port: 8080
    periodSeconds: 5
    failureThreshold: 24   # 2 minutes
  livenessProbe:
    httpGet:
      path: /health
      port: 8080
    periodSeconds: 10
    failureThreshold: 3
  readinessProbe:
    httpGet:
      path: /ready
      port: 8080
    periodSeconds: 5
    failureThreshold: 2

slides.title: When to Use Startup Probes 📌
slides.content:
## Guidelines

- Use when your container’s first startup takes **> initialDelaySeconds + failureThreshold*periodSeconds** of your liveness probe.
- If you don’t define a startup probe, liveness begins after `initialDelaySeconds` (if set) or immediately.
- Startup probes are **one‑shot**: after they succeed once, they never run again for the lifetime of the container.

quizData.question: True or False: A startup probe continues to run periodically after initial success.
quizData.explanation: Once the startup probe succeeds, it is never run again.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Combine startup probe with readiness to hide slow startup from Services

Even if liveness doesn’t start, the Pod won’t get traffic until readiness passes. So a slow startup won’t cause dropped requests – the Pod simply isn’t added to Endpoints.
